To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) customers' efficiency in self-service is positively related to the profitability of the bank and (ii) customers' efficiency is positively related to their use of self-service and negatively related to their use and profitability of traditional channels, which is consistent with the notion that customers' use of self-service channels is a substitute for traditional channels.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how customers use multiple service delivery channels and how their efficiency in service co-production affects firm performance.
the role of customer efficiency as an important determinant of channel utilization and firm performance in multi-channel service delivery systems.
the impact of customer co-production efficiency on the use of self-service channels and its impact on firm performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
customer efficiency is positively associated with firm performance, but that the nature of these associations is complex and depends on the specific channel being used.
customer efficiency is a key driver of customer profitability, and thus should be an important consideration for managers of multi-channel service delivery systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
customer efficiency in self-serve channels is associated with improved firm performance and that the impact of customer efficiency on firm performance is mediated by customer behavior.

customer co-production is a valuable and underutilized resource in service operations and that firms should consider the implications of customer co-production in designing and operating service delivery systems.
customer efficiency in the delivery system can have significant effects on firm performance and that these effects can be quite complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of self-service channels is not simply determined by the number of transactions or the amount of time customers spend in self-service, but also by the efficiency of the customer in using self-service.
customer efficiency in service co-production is an important determinant of firm performance in service industries.
customer efficiency is a key driver of customer behavior and firm performance in a multi-channel environment, and thus should be a central consideration in service operations design and management.
